title: Machine-learning-guided photoredox design experimentally enables three transformations
summary: A workflow combining a variational-autoencoder latent space of 11,069 literature photoredox reactions with random-forest catalyst/reagent recommendations was used to propose three transformations. Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield. The paper presents these as experimentally validated transformations identified through model-assisted precedent retrieval and condition selection.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder for reaction-space navigation and random-forest multilabel catalyst/reagent recommendation
organization: Wuhan University; HOURS Inc.; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield.
evidence.unknown: The work is a human-guided photoredox design workflow, not autonomous synthesis. The three examples were selected by researchers and use a literature-trained model; the paper establishes feasibility for these tested transformations, not general transfer or broad yield improvement. Reported 64% and 74% yields apply only to the specific demonstrated products; further optimization and substrate-scope work are needed.
evidence.ai_role: The VAE organized 11,069 literature-derived reactions to retrieve traceable precedents; random-forest models recommended catalyst and reagent classes for proposed reactant-product pairs. Chemists used the model-suggested conditions to test three transformations, including two modifications beyond the reported precedent and one previously undocumented photoredox synthesis, then measured isolated product yields.
